evidence: The actual KT-02 page interface and the definitions of the chosen exterior and peripheral curves, the full exterior homology/longitude theorem, and the open-to-compact exterior deformation retraction were inspected. These supply the exterior convention, positive meridian, longitude existence/uniqueness, H1 generator, and retraction used by Batch 70. This is an author interface check, not supplier acceptance or independent approval.

The actual KT-05 page, connected-sum/unknot definition, and complete genus-invariance-under-mirror-and-reversal proof were inspected. Batch 70 uses the unknot convention in the unit-slope lemma and the genus invariance result in the sign-reduction step. This is an author interface check, not supplier acceptance or independent approval.

The actual KT-07 page, positive-push Seifert-matrix convention, full determinant theorem proof, and normalization/symmetry/genus-bound corollary proof were inspected. Batch 70 uses the determinant convention and exponent-width bound without changing their hypotheses. This is an author interface check, not supplier acceptance or independent approval.

The actual KT-02 definition fixes the chosen compact exterior as S3 minus the interior of the supplied closed tubular neighborhood, which is the exterior convention stated in the torus-knot definition.

The actual KT-02 definition fixes the positive normal-disk meridian and degree-one null-homologous longitude condition. Batch 70 repeats these roles without claiming existence or uniqueness from the definition alone.
The actual KT-05 definition fixes the standard oriented unknot and orientation-preserving ambient-isotopy convention used to identify the terminal core with the unknot.

The actual KT-04 definition supplies the countable-choice Seifert-surface convention, boundary orientation, and Euler-characteristic genus identity used to identify the constructed band surface as a spanning surface and calculate its genus.
The actual exterior definition supplies the compact exterior and boundary torus used in the Heegaard-annulus decomposition.

The actual peripheral definition supplies the positive normal-disk meridian and degree-one null-homologous longitude conventions. The group proof derives the corresponding words and separately uses the homology theorem for existence and uniqueness.

The complete KT-02 theorem assumes full AC and proves that the positive meridian generates H1(EK;Z), the preferred longitude exists uniquely, and their boundary classes form a basis. Those exact facts fix the meridian sign and identify h mu^(-pq) as the preferred longitude.

The actual KT-02 lemma assumes countable choice and proves that the open complement strongly deformation retracts onto the compact exterior. Full AC supplies that hypothesis; the Alexander-module identification is made only after this retraction is verified.
The complete KT-02 theorem proves the homology generator and identifies the positive-meridian map to Z, which is the epimorphism classifying the infinite cyclic cover in the Fox-module calculation.

The actual KT-04 definition assumes countable choice and defines knot genus as the minimum over connected compact oriented spanning surfaces. The upper/lower-bound argument uses this exact minimum convention.

The complete KT-05 proof assumes countable choice and constructs reflected and orientation-reversed spanning surfaces with unchanged genus in both directions. This justifies reduction to positive absolute parameters.

The full KT-07 theorem proof uses the positive-push convention V_ij=lk(a_i^+,a_j) and identifies the Seifert determinant with the Alexander polynomial under full AC, matching the determinant convention used by the genus-bound corollary.

The complete KT-07 corollary assumes full AC and bounds the exponent width of the Alexander polynomial by twice the minimum knot genus. The formula theorem applies this stated width bound to the explicitly computed polynomial.
